cases.title: FizzBuzz: letzte Zeile fehlt
cases.prompt: `sh fizzbuzz.sh 15` should print 15 lines, the last one being `FizzBuzz`, but the last line is missing. Find and fix the bug.
cases.setup:
cat > fizzbuzz.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# prints FizzBuzz from 1 to $1
n=$1; i=1
while [ $i -lt $n ]; do
  if [ $((i % 15)) -eq 0 ]; then echo FizzBuzz
  elif [ $((i % 3)) -eq 0 ]; then echo Fizz
  elif [ $((i % 5)) -eq 0 ]; then echo Buzz
  else echo $i; fi
  i=$((i + 1))
done
EOF
cases.verify: [ "$(sh fizzbuzz.sh 15 | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = 15 ] && [ "$(sh fizzbuzz.sh 15 | tail -n1)" = FizzBuzz ] && [ "$(sh fizzbuzz.sh 3 | tail -n1)" = Fizz ]

cases.title: Neue Option --shout
cases.prompt: Add a `--shout` option to greet.sh: `sh greet.sh --shout Ann` prints `HELLO, ANN`. Without the option the behaviour stays the same (`sh greet.sh Ann` → `Hello, Ann`, `sh greet.sh` → `Hello, world`).
cases.verify: [ "$(sh greet.sh Ann)" = 'Hello, Ann' ] && [ "$(sh greet.sh --shout Ann)" = 'HELLO, ANN' ] && [ "$(sh greet.sh)" = 'Hello, world' ]
cases.solution:
cat > greet.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
shout=0
if [ "$1" = "--shout" ]; then shout=1; shift; fi
msg="Hello, ${1:-world}"
if [ $shout -eq 1 ]; then echo "$msg" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'; else echo "$msg"; fi
EOF

cases.title: Bedienung dokumentieren
cases.prompt: Document how to use tool.sh in README.md: add a section `## Usage` that explains the `--count N` option with an example.
cases.verify: grep -q '^## Usage' README.md && grep -q -- '--count' README.md && grep -q '# tool' README.md
cases.solution:
printf '
## Usage

    sh tool.sh --count 3

`--count N` prints N lines.
' >> README.md

cases.title: Tests für max.sh schreiben
cases.prompt: Write test_max.sh with at least three test cases for max.sh (it prints the largest of its numeric arguments). The test script must exit non-zero if a case fails.
cases.setup:
cat > max.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
m=$1; for x in "$@"; do [ "$x" -gt "$m" ] && m=$x; done; echo $m
EOF
cases.solution:
cat > test_max.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
set -e
[ "$(sh max.sh 1 2 3)" = 3 ]
[ "$(sh max.sh 7)" = 7 ]
[ "$(sh max.sh -1 -5)" = -1 ]
EOF

cases.title: Doppelte Funktion auslagern
cases.prompt: a.sh and b.sh both define the same `log()` function. Move it into a new file lib.sh and source it from both scripts (`. ./lib.sh`). The output must stay exactly the same.
cases.verify: [ -f lib.sh ] && grep -q 'log()' lib.sh && ! grep -q 'log()' a.sh && ! grep -q 'log()' b.sh && [ "$(sh a.sh)" = '[a] start' ] && [ "$(sh b.sh)" = '[b] start' ]
cases.solution:
printf 'log() { echo "[$1] $2"; }
' > lib.sh
printf '#!/bin/sh
. ./lib.sh
log a start
' > a.sh
printf '#!/bin/sh
. ./lib.sh
log b start
' > b.sh

cases.title: Pfad-Ausbruch verhindern
cases.prompt: readfile.sh prints a file from the data/ folder. It must reject paths that contain `..` or start with `/`: print `invalid path` to stderr and exit with code 2. Valid names keep working.
cases.setup:
mkdir -p data && echo ok > data/x
cat > readfile.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
cat "data/$1"
EOF
cases.verify:
set -e
mkdir -p data; echo ok > data/x
[ "$(sh readfile.sh x)" = ok ]
set +e
sh readfile.sh ../readfile.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; a=$?
sh readfile.sh /etc/passwd >/dev/null 2>&1; b=$?
msg=$(sh readfile.sh ../x 2>&1 >/dev/null)
[ $a -eq 2 ] && [ $b -eq 2 ] && [ "$msg" = 'invalid path' ]

cases.title: Spaltensumme einer CSV
cases.prompt: Write sum.sh: `sh sum.sh FILE` prints the sum of the second column of a CSV file with a header line.
cases.verify: [ "$(sh sum.sh data.csv)" = 60 ] && printf 'n,a\nx,5\n' > /tmp/queue-eval-$$.csv && [ "$(sh sum.sh /tmp/queue-eval-$$.csv)" = 5 ]; r=$?; rm -f /tmp/queue-eval-$$.csv; exit $r

cases.title: Funktion projektweit umbenennen
cases.prompt: Rename the shell function `old_name` to `format_date` everywhere in the project (definition and all callers in every script). All scripts must keep working.
cases.setup:
cat > util.sh <<'EOF'
old_name() { echo "date: $1"; }
EOF
for f in main report export; do printf '#!/bin/sh\n. ./util.sh\nold_name 2026-%s\n' "$f" > $f.sh; done
cases.verify: ! grep -rq old_name --include='*.sh' . && grep -q 'format_date()' util.sh && [ "$(sh main.sh)" = 'date: 2026-main' ] && [ "$(sh export.sh)" = 'date: 2026-export' ]
